data.name: Maddy
data.gender_notes: Maddy is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the names Matilda and Madeline, Maddy is a feminine name with a rich history. Matilda comes from the Germanic elements maht 'might' and hild 'battle'. Madeline is derived from the Hebrew name Magdalene, meaning 'tower of strength'. The name Maddy carries the meaning “Mighty” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Maddy usually hope their child will grow to embody mighty and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of inner strength and resilience.
data.etymology: Maddy belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mighty.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Maddy total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_hebrew.name: מדדי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם מדדי הוא נגזר מהמילים העבריות 'מתנה' ו'אלוהים', ומשמעותו מתנת אלוהים. הוא קשור לשמחה ואושר הנובעים מהמתנות האלוהיות. השם מופיע בהקשרים של ברכה והודיה.

in_greek.name: Μαδή
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Μαδή στην ελληνική παράδοση σχετίζεται με τη χαρά και την ευτυχία. Προέρχεται από τις ρίζες που συνδέονται με τη δωρεά του Θεού και εκφράζει την πνευματική χαρά και την αναψυχή που προέρχεται από την πίστη.

in_latin.name: Maddy
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Maddy in traditione christiana latina significat gaudium et felicitatem. Etymologia nominis connectitur cum donis divinis et exprimit laetitiam spiritualem et recreationem quae ex fide christiana oritur.

in_english.name: Maddy
in_english.long_meaning: The name Maddy is derived from Hebrew roots meaning 'gift of God'. It is associated with joy, happiness, and divine blessings. Historically, names with similar roots have been used in Christian traditions to signify the joy and spiritual gifts received from God. The name Maddy reflects a sense of gratitude and spiritual fulfillment.

data.cultural_impact: The name Maddy has been popularized by numerous high-profile individuals throughout history, with notable figures including Irish author Maud Gonne, English composer Madeline Schroeder, and American actress Madelyn Diana "Maddy" Blair. Its use in popular culture has made it a name recognized across various circles.
data.spiritual_significance: Maddy's roots in the names Matilda and Madeline carry strong meanings of strength, power, and resilience. The name is also connected to the biblical figure Mary Magdalene, who was present at Jesus’ crucifixion, anointed his body with costly perfumes, and was the first person to whom Jesus appeared after his resurrection. As such, the name Maddy is also a reminder of the transformative power of faith and the grace of God.
